title: David Foster
description: Canadian and American record producer and songwriter (born 1949)
wiki_lead:
David Walter Foster (born November 1, 1949) is a Canadian and American record producer, composer, arranger, and musician. He has won 16 Grammy Awards from 45 nominations across four decades (the 1970s, 1980s, 1990s, and 2000s). Since the 1970s, Foster has composed and produced some of the most successful songs of each decade, with multiple songs reaching the top spot on the Billboard Hot 100 and other individual genre charts. He has also been nominated three times in the Best Original song category at the Academy Awards.
Foster has contributed to material for music industry artists across various genres. Some of the songs he has been involved with include: "I Will Always Love You", "I Have Nothing", "The Prayer", "After the Love Has Gone", "Hard to Say I'm Sorry", "Hard Habit to Break", "St. Elmo's Fire (Man in Motion)", "Glory of Love", "Winter Games", "Grown-Up Christmas List", "Best of Me", "Look What You've Done to Me", "She's a Beauty", "Somewhere", and "Wildflower".
Foster served as senior vice president of Warner Music Group from 1997, then he chaired Verve Records from 2012 to 2016.
In the 2020s, Foster composed Boop! The Musical, which premiered in Chicago in 2023 and debuted on Broadway in 2025. He was nominated for a Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Music.

In the 2020s, Foster composed Boop! The Musical, which premiered in Chicago in 2023 and debuted on Broadway in 2025. He was nominated for a Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Music.


Early life
Foster was born in Victoria, British Columbia, the son of Maurice "Maury" Foster (1913–1968), an office worker, and Eleanor May Foster (née Vantreight) (1918–2006), a homemaker. He has six sisters. His parents discovered his perfect pitch at around age three. During his childhood, he studied both classical and jazz music. When he was 13 years old, he heard The Beatles on the radio and was so impressed that he said, "That's what I want to do". In 1963, he enrolled in the University of Washington's music program. He attended Mount Douglas Secondary School from 1964 to 1966. Although he did not graduate, he was awarded his Dogwood Certificate in 1985 and was named Honorary Alumni President in 2010. While attending school, he performed with the local band The Teen Beats, through which he developed a lasting friendship with fellow member Chris Earthy.


Career


1960s
In 1966, he joined a stage band called The Strangers, and soon afterward they moved to London. They performed with Chuck Berry and Bo Diddley. Diddley became a mentor to Foster, teaching him about groove. During this time, Foster was going through a difficult period, and was barely able to make ends meet.
In 1969, he auditioned for a band at a nightclub in Edmonton owned by jazz musician Tommy Banks. Banks mentored Foster in jazz, producing records, and the music business. Around the same time, Foster also performed with Ronnie Hawkins.

grok_lead: David Walter Foster OC OBC (born November 1, 1949) is a Canadian record producer, composer, arranger, and musician recognized for his extensive work in pop and adult contemporary genres. Born in Victoria, British Columbia, Foster started piano lessons at age five, which sparked his early musical development leading to formal studies and a professional trajectory in songwriting and production. His career highlights include co-writing Earth, Wind & Fire's " After the Love Has Gone," which earned him his first Grammy Award in 1979 for Best R&B Song, and producing multiplatinum albums for artists like Chicago, whose 1984 release Chicago 17 yielded several hits and Grammy wins for Foster as Producer of the Year, Non-Classical. Foster has collaborated with Whitney Houston on tracks like " I Have Nothing " and Celine Dion on "The Power of Love," contributing to soundtracks such as St. Elmo's Fire and earning a total of 16 Grammy Awards across categories including Album of the Year for Natalie Cole's Unforgettable... with Love in 1992. As a music executive, he chaired Verve Records from 2012 to 2016 and has received honors like induction into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame for his commercial successes and influence on contemporary hit-making.
